calcPage.reason1: Cables that are too thin become dangerously hot
calcPage.seoTitle1: How to calculate the right cable size?
calcPage.seoText1: The right cable size is essential for a safe and efficient 12V or 24V installation in your campervan. A cable that is too thin leads to excessive voltage drop, overheating and in the worst case, fire hazard. By entering the power (Watt) or current (Ampère), cable length and desired maximum voltage drop, our tool calculates the minimum cross-section you need.
calcPage.seoText1b: We use the standard copper conductor formula with a conductivity of 56 m/Ω·mm². The cable length is automatically doubled to account for both the positive and negative conductors. This way you always get reliable advice, whether you're connecting a small fridge or a heavy inverter.
calcPage.seoTitle2: Watt vs. Ampère — what's the difference?
calcPage.seoText2: Watt (W) is the total power consumed by a device, while Ampère (A) is the current flowing through the cable. The relationship is simple: Watt = Volt × Ampère. In a 12V system, a 600W device draws 50A. At 24V it's only 25A — that's why 24V systems are popular at higher powers, as you can use thinner cables.
calcPage.tip1: Always choose the next standard cable size above the calculated minimum — one size larger is safer.
calcPage.tip2: Keep cables as short as possible to limit voltage drop, and bundle positive and negative cables together for a neat installation.
calcPage.tip3: Place a fuse as close to the battery as possible — it protects the cable, not the device.

about.introText2: From Belgium, we support campervan builders across Europe with honest advice, tested products and personal WhatsApp support. No call center, no waiting — just us.
about.storyText1: It all started with a van and a dream. Like many vanlifers, we just wanted to hit the road — free and independent. But when converting our first campervan, we discovered how difficult it was to find reliable 12V components without paying a premium.

powerSeo.title1: How to calculate your campervan power consumption?
powerSeo.text1: Daily power consumption in a campervan is measured in watt-hours (Wh). Calculate it by multiplying each appliance's power (in Watts) by the hours you use it per day. For example, a 10W LED light running 4 hours consumes 40Wh per day.
powerSeo.text1b: By adding up all your appliances, you get your total daily consumption. Based on that, you determine the required battery capacity. A LiFePO4 battery offers about 80% usable capacity (e.g. 200Ah × 12.8V × 0.8 = ±2,048Wh), while an AGM battery only provides 50% usable capacity.
powerSeo.title2: LiFePO4 vs AGM — how much capacity do you really need?
powerSeo.text2: A common mistake is comparing LiFePO4 and AGM capacity one-to-one. AGM batteries should only be discharged to 50% to preserve lifespan, while LiFePO4 can be discharged to 80-90%. A 200Ah LiFePO4 battery provides as much usable energy as a 400Ah AGM battery — at half the weight.
powerSeo.tip1: Choose 12V appliances over 230V where possible — an inverter always costs 10-15% energy.
powerSeo.tip2: Solar panels (100-400Wp) can significantly reduce your daily consumption and double your autonomy.
powerSeo.tip3: Monitor your consumption with a battery monitor — this prevents unexpectedly running out of power.

buildSeo.title1: How to choose the right off-grid package?
buildSeo.text1: The ideal energy system depends on three factors: how you use your camper (weekend vs. full-time), which appliances you want to power, and whether you have solar panels. A weekend camper with LED lighting and a phone needs a very different system than a full-timer with a fridge, laptop and coffee maker.
buildSeo.text1b: Our package generator combines these factors and automatically calculates the optimal battery capacity and inverter for your situation. This way you know for sure you're not over- or under-investing.
buildSeo.title2: What's in a complete campervan energy system?
buildSeo.text2: An off-grid energy system for your campervan consists of several components working together:
buildSeo.comp1: LiFePO4 battery (100-300Ah) — the core of your system, stores all energy
buildSeo.comp2: Inverter (1000-3000W) — converts 12V to 230V for household appliances
buildSeo.comp3: Cables (correct thickness!) — connect everything safely, cables that are too thin are a fire hazard
buildSeo.comp4: Fuses & distribution blocks — protect your installation against short circuits
buildSeo.faq1q: Can I upgrade my system later?
buildSeo.faq1a: Yes! LiFePO4 batteries can be connected in parallel. Start with 200Ah and add a second battery later if you need more capacity.
buildSeo.faq2a: Only if you want to use 230V appliances (coffee maker, hair dryer, etc.). Many campervan appliances run directly on 12V, so an inverter isn't always necessary.
buildSeo.faq3q: How long does a LiFePO4 battery last?
buildSeo.faq3a: LiFePO4 batteries last 3,000 to 5,000 charge cycles — that's 8 to 15 years with daily use. By comparison, an AGM battery averages 300-500 cycles.
